tasks.corrected_reference_answer: The source shows potential cumulative overhead, not a demonstrated scaling bottleneck. Benchmark combinations span problems, starts, software, minimizers, Jacobians and Hessians (fitbenchmarking/core/fitting_benchmarking.py:40-49). Each eval_model calls check_elapsed_time (fitbenchmarking/parsing/fitting_problem.py:126-143), which reads the clock while the timer is active and compares cumulative elapsed time against max_runtime (fitbenchmarking/utils/timer.py:50-61). More fit evaluations imply more checks, but profiling would be needed to establish their cost relative to fitting. The resets at fitting_benchmarking.py:577-578 and 610-611 protect completed results and clear timer state after exception handling; the source does not show they are redundant.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: For multiple present grouping variables, GroupBy._get_groups constructs pd.MultiIndex.from_product from their level orders (seaborn/_core/groupby.py:49-70). If their cardinalities are k1 through km, that index has product(ki) entries even when few combinations occur. agg groups with observed=True but then reindexes to this complete index, adding rows for absent combinations (groupby.py:79-100). apply also constructs the index and iterates its combinations (groupby.py:105-126). This can add substantial work and memory for sparse high-cardinality inputs. Plot.pair additionally stores separate statistical outputs per coordinate pair (seaborn/_core/plot.py:1234-1238; seaborn/_core/data.py:64-69), but the source alone does not quantify copying or establish that this is the dominant bottleneck.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: SQLFluff already reuses grammar definitions: dialect.ref returns a library element, and Ref.match delegates to it (src/sqlfluff/core/dialects/base.py:285-299; src/sqlfluff/core/parser/grammar/base.py:407-427). Matching returns MatchResult and can reuse a segment of the required class (src/sqlfluff/core/parser/segments/base.py:618-645). Later MatchResult.apply recursively builds the selected tree and constructs matched classes (src/sqlfluff/core/parser/match_result.py:193-200,257-282), using from_result_segments (segments/base.py:1233-1239). Each new node stores its own children, UUID, marker and parent/cache state (segments/base.py:194-212), so more nested nodes imply additional objects and initialization work. Grammar objects cannot directly replace these occurrence-specific nodes. Additional GC cost is plausible but unmeasured; the source does not establish a bottleneck, and construction is already deferred until apply.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: Response.apparent_encoding checks chardet is not None at src/requests/models.py:792. compat._resolve_char_detection first tries chardet then charset_normalizer (src/requests/compat.py:30-42). If neither is available, apparent_encoding returns utf-8 without accessing self.content (models.py:794-797). With a detector, it evaluates self.content and returns detect(...)["encoding"] (792-793). content returns cached bytes or lazily consumes iter_content into bytes, with special error/None cases (890-907). A detector returning encoding=None produces None here; a detector exception propagates. Neither case is converted to utf-8 by apparent_encoding, so missing-library fallback and detection failure are different control-flow cases.
